name: openchase
description: See what publications and people are posting right now on X, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and more, and build OpenChase search into your own code.

interface.longDescription: Search recent public posts and articles across social platforms and publications. Find reactions to people, companies, products, and events, then open selected results with links to their original sources.
defaultPrompt: What are people saying about OpenAI today?
Find recent Reddit posts about electric vehicles.
Show recent reactions to the latest product launch.

publication.release_notes: OpenChase 1.0.1: search what people and publications are posting right now on X, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Threads, Facebook, Substack, Medium and news sites, by country and time window. Get the original links for the posts you cite and read an article's full text when its title isn't enough. Sign in with an OpenChase account; new accounts get 10 free credits.

positive.description: Country and time window: recent conversation about a company in one country
positive.prompt: What are people in India saying about Reliance Jio in the last 24 hours?
positive.expected_behavior: Searches India (countries: in) over the last 24 hours on several platforms including publications, then summarizes what each platform is saying with the posts it draws on, and offers to fetch links.

positive.description: Named platforms over a week, both positive and negative reactions
positive.prompt: How are people on X and Reddit reacting to Tesla this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Searches only X and Reddit over the last 7 days and gives separate takes for each platform, covering both positive and negative reactions where they exist.

positive.description: Publication coverage in one country, with links to the sources
positive.prompt: What are UK publications reporting about the Bank of England today? Include the links.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches publications in the UK (countries: gb) over the last 24 hours, then fetches the original links for the articles it cites and returns a short summary with those links.

positive.description: Deep read of one article when the headline isn't enough
positive.prompt: Find a recent news article about the Bank of England and tell me what it actually says.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches publications, then reads one publication result's page text and summarizes the article's own content, with its link.

positive.prompt: How many OpenChase credits do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the signed-in account's name and remaining credits. No purchase or checkout link.

negative.description: Scraping a given URL: OpenChase searches topics and has no tool that takes a URL, so it should explain that rather than try to work around it.
negative.prompt: Scrape every comment from https://www.reddit.com/r/india/comments/abc123/ and list all the usernames.

negative.description: Locating a private person: OpenChase is for public conversation about topics, not for finding someone's home address or phone number, so it should decline without searching.
negative.prompt: Find the home address and phone number of my neighbour Priya Sharma in Bangalore.

negative.description: Buying credits inside ChatGPT: there is no purchase tool and ChatGPT doesn't sell credits, so it should say buying isn't possible here and at most point to the informational page openchase.ai/pricing, never a checkout.
negative.prompt: Buy 10,000 more OpenChase credits for me.

review.commerce_description: Nothing is sold inside ChatGPT. Credits are bought on openchase.ai; inside ChatGPT the plugin at most links to the informational pricing page.
